title: Conjectured formula for the uniformly dense Turán density of stars
classification_reason: The star and precise uniform-density convention are only referenced.
literal_statement_utf8:
For each integer $k$ with $4\le k\le 10$, let $S_k$ denote the star $3$-graph considered in the paper, and let $\pi_{\mathrm{U}}(S_k)$ be its uniformly dense Turán density. **Conjecture for stars.**

$$
\pi_{\mathrm{U}}(S_k)=\frac{k^2-5k+7}{(k-1)^2}\quad\text{for all }4\le k\le 10.
$$

The paper proves the same formula for $k\ge 11$ and, for the related notion represented by $\pi_{\mathrm{V}}$, for $k\ge 5$; the uniformly dense cases $4\le k\le 10$ remain conjectural.
quantifier_scope: Every integer k=4,...,10; exact rational density.
technical_assessment: Seven parameters do not make the hypergraph density optimization finite: both upper and lower density proofs are needed. No certified extremal reduction identified.

title: The homological connectivity threshold conjecture for k-fold coverage
classification_reason: The sampling law, coefficient field for homology, radius-intensity relation and complex construction are absent.
literal_statement_utf8:
Let $B_r^{(k)}$ be the $k$-fold coverage complex on the $d$-dimensional torus, let ${\cal{H}}_{i,r}^{(k)}$ be the event that $H_i(B_s^{(k)})\cong H_i({\mathbb{T}}^d)$ for every $s\geq r$, and let $\Lambda$ be the model's intensity parameter. Let $k\geq 1$ and $0\leq i\leq d-2$, and suppose that $w(n)\rightarrow\infty$ as $n\rightarrow\infty$.

**Homological connectivity threshold conjecture.**

$$
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{P}({\cal{H}}_{i,r}^{(k)}) = \begin{cases} 1 & \Lambda = \log n + (i+k-2)\log\log n + w(n), \\ 0 & \Lambda = \log n + (i+k-2)\log\log n - w(n). \end{cases}
$$

The preceding corollary gives only an upper bound for these homological connectivity thresholds, while the conjecture is motivated by the homological connectivity results of Bobrowski (2022).
quantifier_scope: All k>=1,0<=i<=d-2 and w(n) tending to infinity; two limiting probability claims.
technical_assessment: An upper threshold does not supply the lower threshold; expected critical points alone would not control persistent homology for every later radius.

title: The good-prime congruence for meromorphic modular forms with elliptic-curve poles
classification_reason: Standard normalized Eisenstein series and j invariant specify the coefficients and all curve/prime restrictions are given.
literal_statement_utf8:
Let $C/\mathbb{Q}$ be an elliptic curve with $j(C)\notin\{0,1728\}$, and write

$$
F_{k,C}:=\frac{E_k}{j-j(C)}=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}a_n(F_{k,C})q^n,
$$

where $k\in\{4,6,8,10,14\}$. Let $p$ be a good prime of $C$, with $v_p(j(C))=0=v_p(j(C)-1728)$. **The good-prime congruence.** For all $n\in\mathbb{Z}^+$,

$$
a_{np}(F_{k,C})\equiv a_p(C)^{k-2}a_n(F_{k,C})\pmod p.
$$

The source notes that this is a theorem when $p\geq5$, so the conjectural formulation is solved.
quantifier_scope: Every stated elliptic curve, k in {4,6,8,10,14}, good p with two valuation restrictions, and n>=1.
technical_assessment: Actual source Remark2.2 and Theorem5.1 prove the p>=5 range; Section5.4 explicitly gives only a hypergeometric proof sketch. Small primes require a domain check, not new discovery credit. No independent full dependency replay.

evidence.primary: Selected question/definition/theorem and Section5.4 proof sketch; not whole body. Theorem5.1 p>=5 scope only; hypergeometric machinery and all local lemmas not replayed. Higher-order CM definitions only partial.

title: The CM magnetic divisibility conjecture for higher-order poles
classification_reason: Having a pole of order r does not uniquely select an integral linear combination G; its normalization is missing.
literal_statement_utf8:
Let $G_{k,D}^{(r)}$ denote the integral linear combination of $E_k/(j-j(\alpha_D))^i$ for $1\leq i\leq r$ having a pole of order $r$ at the CM point of discriminant $D$. Let $k\in\{4,6,8,10,14\}$, $1\leq r\leq k-1$, and set $r'=\min(r,k-r)$. Let $D<-4$ be a discriminant with class number $1$. **The CM magnetic divisibility conjecture.** The form $G_{k,D}^{(r)}$ is $(r'-1)$-magnetic: for every $n\in\mathbb{Z}^+$,

$$
n^{r'-1}\mid a_n(G_{k,D}^{(r)}).
$$

This predicts systematic divisibility of Fourier coefficients in the CM family; the source presents it as a numerical conjecture and does not establish it in general.
quantifier_scope: Every listed k,1<=r<=k-1,class-number-one D<-4,n>=1; n^(min(r,k-r)-1) divides coefficient.
technical_assessment: Need the distinguished coefficient choices before any computation. r'=1 yields tautological divisibility; that is no route to the nontrivial orders or a credited outcome.

evidence.primary: Selected question/definition/theorem and Section5.4 proof sketch; not whole body. Theorem5.1 p>=5 scope only; hypergeometric machinery and all local lemmas not replayed. Higher-order CM definitions only partial.

title: The complementary-pole coefficient-product divisibility conjecture
classification_reason: The CM forms G are named without their coefficient choices.
literal_statement_utf8:
Let $G_{k,D}^{(r)}$ be the CM higher-order-pole forms, let $k\in\{4,6,8,10,14\}$, $1\leq r\leq k-1$, and let $D<-4$ be a discriminant with class number $1$. **The complementary-pole divisibility conjecture.** For every $n\in\mathbb{Z}^+$,

$$
n^{k-2}\mid a_n(G_{k,D}^{(r)})a_n(G_{k,D}^{(k-r)}).
$$

This is a numerical divisibility phenomenon for complementary pole orders in the CM family and remains open.
quantifier_scope: Every listed k,r,D and n>=1; coefficient product divisible by n^(k-2).
technical_assessment: Separate divisibilities with exponent min(r,k-r)-1 do not give the required product exponent; no uniform prime-adic mechanism established.

title: The 1/3-2/3 conjecture for linear extensions
classification_reason: Uniform linear extensions, pair probabilities and the nonchain domain are explicit.
literal_statement_utf8:
Let $P$ be a finite poset. For distinct elements $x,y\in P$, define

$$
\delta_{xy}=\min\{\mathbb{P}(x\prec y),\mathbb{P}(y\prec x)\},
$$

and let

$$
\delta(P)=\max_{x\ne y}\delta_{xy},
$$

where the probabilities are taken over a uniformly random linear extension of $P$. **The 1/3-2/3 conjecture.** If $P$ is not a chain, then $\delta(P)\geq 1/3$. This conjecture is motivated by sorting problems; the bound is known to be tight, but the conjectured constant $1/3$ remains unresolved, with the best stated general lower bound being $(5-\sqrt{5})/10$.
quantifier_scope: Every finite nonchain poset contains a distinct pair with both ordering probabilities >=1/3.
technical_assessment: A balance argument for a special width or a local swap does not control arbitrary posets. No full-scope route or short counterexample certificate identified.

title: Mascia–Rinaldo–Romeo primality conjecture for polyomino ideals
classification_reason: Zig-zag walk and the generators of the cell ideal require the source.
literal_statement_utf8:
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a polyomino, and let $I_{\mathcal{P}}$ be its polyomino ideal. A **zig–zag walk** is the combinatorial configuration defined earlier in the source. The rank of $\mathcal{P}$ is the number of its cells.

**Mascia–Rinaldo–Romeo conjecture.** The following conditions are equivalent:

1. $I_{\mathcal{P}}$ is a prime ideal.
2. $\mathcal{P}$ contains no zig–zag walk.

The equivalence is known for polyominoes of rank at most $14$, based on systematic enumeration and computation. The conjecture asserts that the zig–zag obstruction is the only obstruction to primality in arbitrary rank.
quantifier_scope: Every polyomino, arbitrary rank; primality iff no zig-zag walk.
technical_assessment: Need a global saturation or normal-form argument; finite low-rank ideal computations cannot establish the equivalence.

title: Navarra–Qureshi–Rinaldo domino-stability conjecture for Gorenstein cell ideals
classification_reason: Domino stability and the coordinate-ring construction are omitted.
literal_statement_utf8:
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a collection of cells, and let $K[\mathcal{P}]$ be its coordinate ring. A collection of cells is **domino-stable** when it has the domino-stability property defined in the source.

**Domino-stability conjecture.** The ring $K[\mathcal{P}]$ is Gorenstein if and only if $\mathcal{P}$ is domino-stable.

Domino stability is known to characterize palindromicity of the switching rook polynomial, and computational evidence proves the Gorenstein conclusion for domino-stable collections of rank at most $10$ and domino-stable polyominoes of rank at most $12$. title: Sun's classification conjecture for suitable two-variable linear polynomials
classification_reason: N includes zero in some conventions; four-square suitability depends on that convention.
literal_statement_utf8:
Let $P(X,Y,Z,W)\in\mathbb{Z}[X,Y,Z,W]$ be called **suitable** if, for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, there exist $x,y,z,w\in\mathbb{N}$ such that

$$
\begin{cases}
 n=x^2+y^2+z^2+w^2,\\
 P(x,y,z,w)\in\mathcal{S},
\end{cases}
$$

where $\mathcal{S}=\{x^2:x\in\mathbb{Z}\}$. **Sun's classification conjecture.** Let $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}^+$ with $\gcd(a,b)$ square-free and $a\leq b$. Then $aX+bY$ is suitable if and only if

$$
(a,b)=(1,2),(1,3),(1,24).
$$

This conjecture classifies the two-variable linear forms that always occur as a square within a four-square representation of every positive integer. The supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.
quantifier_scope: All positive a<=b with square-free gcd; suitability for every n iff one of three pairs.
technical_assessment: Both universal sufficiency for three forms and exclusion of all other coefficient pairs are required. A finite n obstruction search alone would be incomplete.

title: Zywina's conjecture on possible adelic indices of non-CM elliptic curves
classification_reason: Literal base field is printed as 4Q; correcting it to Q is interpretive.
literal_statement_utf8:
Let $E$ be a non-CM elliptic curve over $4\mathbb{Q}$, let $G_E$ denote its adelic Galois image, and define the finite set

$$
\mathcal{I}=\left\{2,4,6,8,10,12,16,20,24,30,32,36,40,48,54,60,72,80,84,96,108,112,120,128,144,160,182,192,200,216,220,224,240,288,300,336,360,384,480,504,576,768,864,1152,1200,1296,1536,2736\right\}.
$$

**Zywina's conjecture.** The adelic index satisfies

$$
[\operatorname{GL}_2(\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}):G_E]\in\mathcal{I}.
$$

The conjecture predicts a complete finite list of adelic indices for non-CM elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$. It has been verified for all such curves currently in the LMFDB, but remains unproved in general and is closely connected with Serre's uniformity question.

title: The optimal linear bound for zero-sum Ramsey numbers of forests
classification_reason: Zero-sum Ramsey number, forests, divisibility and eventual threshold are explicit.
literal_statement_utf8:
Let $p$ be prime, let $n_p=n(p)$ be a positive integer, and let $F$ be a forest on $n\geq n_p$ vertices such that $p\mid e(F)$. Here $R(F,\mathbb{Z}_p)$ denotes the least order of a complete graph such that every edge-coloring by $\mathbb{Z}_p$ contains a zero-sum copy of $F$. **The optimal forest bound.** For every prime $p$, there is a positive integer $n_p=n(p)$ such that

$$
R(F,\mathbb{Z}_p)\leq n+p-1.
$$

The paper proves the weaker bound $R(F,\mathbb{Z}_p)\leq n+9p-12$ for forests with $n\geq 3p^2-12p+11$, while constructions show that the additive constant cannot be smaller than $p-1$.
quantifier_scope: For each prime p exists n_p such that every n>=n_p forest with p dividing e(F) has R<=n+p-1.
technical_assessment: A fixed-prime or bounded-tree construction does not give the uniform eventual forest embedding. The additive improvement needs a new full-scope embedding mechanism.

title: Link–knot defect proportion comparison conjecture
classification_reason: Crossing number, prime alternating knots/links and the two compared proportions are standard invariants.
literal_statement_utf8:
For a prime alternating knot or link $K$, let $\gamma(K)$ denote its crosscap number and let $\Gamma(K)$ denote its unoriented genus. At crossing number $c$, compare the proportions of prime alternating links and knots satisfying $\gamma>\Gamma$.

**Defect proportion comparison conjecture.** For all even $c\geq 4$ and all odd $c\geq 11$, the proportion of $c$-crossing prime alternating links $L$ with $\gamma(L)>\Gamma(L)$ is larger than the proportion of $c$-crossing prime alternating knots $K$ with $\gamma(K)>\Gamma(K)$.

The conjecture is motivated by the heuristic that links have more two-sided state surfaces, together with an observed parity-dependent emergence in the data. Its status is open.
quantifier_scope: Every even c>=4 and odd c>=11; link defect proportion strictly exceeds knot proportion.
technical_assessment: A low-crossing violation could refute it, but no exact complete census is bound here. Asymptotic heuristics would not cover all stated crossing numbers.

title: Rational Angle Conjecture for maximal volume ideal polyhedra
classification_reason: The ambient geometry and admissible volume-maximization space are not explicitly fixed.
literal_statement_utf8:
Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a realizable triangulation of the sphere, and consider the volume-maximizing ideal polyhedron with combinatorial type $\mathcal{T}$. **Rational Angle Conjecture.** All of its dihedral angles have the form

$$
\frac{p\pi}{q}
$$

for integers $p$ and $q$. The optimization problem has no built-in preference for rational angles, and the phenomenon has been verified for the globally maximal configurations with $n=4,\ldots,12$, but remains unproved for every realizable triangulation.
quantifier_scope: Every realizable sphere triangulation; every maximizing dihedral angle rational times pi.
technical_assessment: Generic algebraic critical points suggest an obstruction but do not certify irrationality at an actual global maximum. Needs exact convex-program and arithmetic certificate, not decimal angles.

title: The nice-knot characterization conjecture

title: The modulo-10 Collatz conjecture
classification_reason: The integer map and target 4 are explicit in every residue class.
literal_statement_utf8: For a positive integer $n\geq1$, if $n$ is a multiple of $10$, replace it by $n/10$; otherwise, let $r$ be its last digit, replace it by $(12n+8r)/10$, and iterate this process. **Modulo-10 Collatz conjecture.** For every starting integer $n\geq1$, the process eventually reaches $4$ after finitely many iterations. This is the paper's first generalized Collatz example and is presented as a conjecture supported by preliminary computational verification; no proof is supplied.
quantifier_scope: Every positive starting integer eventually hits 4.
technical_assessment: For n=10q+r with r>0 the next value is 12q+2r, often larger than n; elementary descent fails. Source Section4.1 is finite verification, not termination for all integers.

evidence.primary: Keyword-selected lines on Conjecture1.3 and Section4.1 finite verification, not continuous primary-question passage or proof-body clearance. Literal map alone screened.

title: Self-reciprocity conjecture for the partial Hasse polynomials of the double cover of $W_{17}$
classification_reason: Partial Hasse polynomials and their normalization on the cover are not constructed.
literal_statement_utf8:
Let $\Pi_{17}$ be the double cover of the Teichmüller curve $W_{17}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{H}^2/\mathrm{SL}(\mathcal{O}_{17}\oplus\mathcal{O}^{\vee}_{17})$. For $j\in\{1,2\}$ and every prime $p\ne 2,17$, let $\mathrm{ph}^{\Pi_{17}}_{p,j}(J)$ be the corresponding partial Hasse polynomial, and let $n_{p,j}$ be the degree of $\mathrm{ph}_{p,j}$. **Self-reciprocity conjecture.** The partial Hasse polynomials satisfy

$$
\mathrm{ph}^{\Pi_{17}}_{p,j}(J)=\mathrm{ph}^{\Pi_{17}}_{p,j}(J^{-1})\cdot J^{n_{p,j}}.
$$

The conjecture asserts reciprocal symmetry for the partial Hasse polynomials in the computed degree-two cover of $W_{17}$. The source reports that this property holds in the cases computed and conjectures that it holds in general, but gives no proof or resolution.
quantifier_scope: Every prime p other than2,17 and j=1,2; coefficient reciprocity of degree n_pj.
technical_assessment: A cover involution might act on the Hasse section with a scalar; normalization and two embeddings must be tracked. No full functorial bridge proved.

title: Miller et al.'s conjecture on infinite square-free digit walks
classification_reason: Square-freeness and decimal append recurrence are fully specified.
literal_statement_utf8:
For a positive integer $N$, define the right-append map by

$$
T_d(N)=10N+d,
$$

where $d\in\{0,1,\dots,9\}$. A positive integer is **square-free** if it is not divisible by any perfect square greater than $1$.

**Miller et al.'s conjecture.** There exists an infinite sequence of square-free integers

$$
\{N_0,N_1,N_2,N_3,\dots\}
$$

and digits $d_{k+1}\in\{0,1,\dots,9\}$ such that

$$
N_{k+1}=10N_k+d_{k+1}
$$

for all $k\geq 0$.

This asks whether one can continue a square-free walk indefinitely by successively appending decimal digits. The question was raised by Miller et al.; despite the result in the paper being previously obtained by Mirsky in 1947, the stated conjecture remains open.
quantifier_scope: Exists an infinite square-free append path with digits0,...,9 and positive N0.
technical_assessment: Arbitrarily large square-free integers do not supply a single compatible prefix path. A counting/sieve extension valid at every surviving prefix is missing.

title: Asymptotics for higher moments of random polyhedral cone angles

m(d,k) \sim \frac{c_k}{2^d\cdot d}

title: Hegedüs' conjecture on skew Bollobás systems of projective subspaces
classification_reason: Intersection requirements, arbitrary field and dimension are explicit; projective subspaces use the standard nonempty convention.
literal_statement_utf8:
Let $W$ be an $n$-dimensional projective space over an arbitrary field $\mathbb{F}$, and let $\mathcal{P}=\{(A_i,B_i)\}_{i=1}^m$ be a **skew Bollobás system** of projective subspaces of $W$, meaning that

$$
A_i\cap B_i=\emptyset \quad\text{for every }i\in [m],
$$

and

$$
A_i\cap B_j\neq\emptyset \quad\text{for all }1\leq i<j\leq m.
$$

**Hegedüs' conjecture.** Every such system satisfies

$$
m\leq 2^{\,n+1}-2.

title: Gallardo–Grekos–Pihko conjecture on three-fold restricted sumsets
classification_reason: Odd cyclic group, restricted triple sums and absolute additive constant are explicit.
literal_statement_utf8:
Let $n$ be an odd positive integer, let $\mathbb{Z}_n$ be the cyclic group of order $n$, and let $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_n$. Write $3^\wedge A$ for the set of sums of three distinct elements of $A$:

$$
3^\wedge A=\{a_1+a_2+a_3:a_i\in A,\ a_i\ne a_j\text{ for }i\ne j\}.
$$

**Gallardo–Grekos–Pihko conjecture.** There is a constant $c$ such that, whenever

$$
|A|>\frac{2}{5}n+c,
$$

one has

$$
3^\wedge A=\mathbb{Z}_n.
$$

Earlier results establish the conclusion for larger density thresholds, including $|A|>n/2$ for all integers $n\geq12$ except $n=15$, while the stated $2/5$ threshold remains the conjectural target.

technical_assessment: Subgroup/coset obstructions dictate the2/5 threshold; prime-order restricted-sum estimates do not automatically treat composite n uniformly. No full structural proof.

title: Banerjee–Bringmann–Bachraoui's family of congruence conjectures for two-color partition numbers

$$
c\left(2^{2k+3}n+\frac{11\cdot 4^{k}+1}{3}\right)\equiv 0\pmod 4,
$$

$$
c\left(2^{2k+3}n+\frac{17\cdot 4^{k}+1}{3}\right)\equiv 0\pmod 8,
$$

and

c\left(2^{2k+4}n+\frac{38\cdot 4^{k}+1}{3}\right)\equiv 0\pmod 4.

title: Dennin's coefficient-positivity conjecture for Grothendieck pattern coefficients
classification_reason: Principal specialization and beta sign convention for the Grothendieck polynomial are omitted.

Here $p_v(w)$ counts occurrences of the permutation pattern $v$ in $w$.

**Dennin's conjecture.** For every permutation $w$,

$$
c_w(\beta)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}[\beta].
$$

Equivalently,

$$
\Upsilon_w(\beta)=\sum_v c_v(\beta)p_v(w),\qquad c_v(\beta)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}[\beta].
$$
